programme.title: Florence Nightingale: Nursing Pioneer
programme.desc: A look at the life of Florence Nightingale, a trailblazer who revolutionised modern nursing. Born into a rich English family, Nightingale broke through social and gender barriers to pioneer a profession previously reserved for men.

programme.title: From Ice to Fire: The Incredible Science of Temperature
programme.desc: Dr Helen Czerski ventures to the bottom of the temperature scale, revealing how cold has shaped the world around us and why frozen doesn't mean what you might think.

programme.title: The Ruth Ellis Files: A Very British Crime Story
programme.desc: In April 1955 Ruth Ellis shot her lover David Blakely dead. It's a case that shocked the nation and it still fascinates today. It has its place in ushering in the defence of diminished responsibility and the abolishment of capital punishment.

programme.title: The Perfect Morecambe & Wise
programme.desc: Eric dons a wig and Tom Jones performs 'Exactly Like You' with some unlikely backing singers. Eric and Ernie take on the strange case of Dr Jekyll & Mr Hyde with Dame Judi Dench and the boys get musical in 'There is Nothin' Like a Dame'.

programme.title: Five to Eleven
programme.desc: Judi Dench reads `The Cultivation of Christmas Trees' by TS Eliot and `The Cherry Tree Carol Poem' by Anon.

programme.title: The Miracle Club
programme.desc: There's just one dream for the women of Ballygar to taste freedom: to win a pilgrimage to the sacred French town of Lourdes. With a little benevolent interference from their local priest, a group of close friends get their ticket of a lifetime.

programme.title: Personal Cinema: Maggie Smith
programme.desc: In a programme first broadcast in 1970, Maggie Smith talks to Michael Aspel about her career and chooses scenes from some of her favourite films, including Way Out West, The Last Hurrah, On the Waterfront, Some Like It Hot and The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie.

programme.title: Tea With Mussolini
programme.desc: Florence 1935. A circle of English ladies settled in the cultured city take an orphan boy, Luca, under their wing. But even a propaganda encounter with Il Duce cannot protect them when war comes, and it falls to Luca and two brash American women they barely tolerate to ease their existence.

programme.title: How to Get Ahead
programme.desc: Stephen Smith explores the flamboyant Baroque court of the Sun King, Louis XIV. Louis created the Palace of Versailles so he could surround himself with aristocrats, artists, interior designers, gardeners, wigmakers, chefs and musicians. Hordes of ambitious courtiers scrambled to get close to the king, but unseemly goings-on in the royal bedchamber reflected the quickest path to power.

programme.title: Hot Chocolate at the BBC
programme.desc: Errol Brown, who died aged 71 in May 2015, was probably the most famous and ubiquitous black British pop star of the 70s and early 80s. This compilation of BBC performances and rare interview extracts celebrates Errol and 'Hot Chocolate', showcasing their top ten hits alongside rarely seen early performances and cult fan favourites.

programme.title: When Bob Marley Came to Britain
programme.desc: Featuring rarely-seen archive and interviews with people who met him, this documentary examines Marley's special relationship with Britain and reveals how his presence helped influence British politics, culture and identity during a time of massive social and civil unrest in the UK, and how his universal message of one love and unity helped inspire a generation of Black British youth.

programme.title: Bob Marley Reimagined

programme.title: Ian Hislop Goes off the Rails
programme.desc: Ian Hislop has a look at the notorious Beeching Report of 1963, which led to the closure of a third of the nation's railway lines and stations and forced tens of thousands of people into the car and onto the road. He investigates the fallout from the plan, discovering what was lost to the British landscape, communities and ways of life when the railway map shrank.
